finding.summary: @lenticule-science/metrologic/chu held a second implementation of Chu spaces over FOUR (chu.mjs) and of the Chu(FOUR) category (chu-transform.mjs), duplicating @lenticule-science/articulating/predicating/positing/logic/linear-logic-chu, the executable form of Obsmetrologia/Calculus/Logic/LinearLogicChu.lean. chu/src/four.mjs was NOT a duplicate: it already delegated every operation to the canonical bilattice-charge morphisms and is a legitimate vocabulary view (Belnap's t/f/bot/top over the canonical potential/active/absurd/stable).
finding.whyCanonical: linear-logic-chu is Lean-grounded, stores a dense charge matrix (so dual(dual(C)) = C holds as a structural equality a closure-valued matrix cannot witness), and its entries are charge carriers that carry their evidence. The metrologic copy was closure-valued, FOUR-string-valued, and evidence-free.

kept.reason: a vocabulary VIEW for a mathematics-facing audience, not a second algebra: every operation lifts a bilattice-charge morphism through the name table and re-derives nothing. Its only consumers after this pass are metrologic's own verdier/gauge.mjs and dframe/cohomology.mjs.

breaking: the ./chu, ./chu/chu and ./chu/transform exports are gone; number.asExtension now returns a linearLogicChu.space
breaking: every FOUR-valued face it emits is now a canonical charge-value name
breaking: section.settled and chuRead.cells[].value now carry canonical charge-value names

openObligations.severity: blocking for the two public game faces at repin time; inert until then
openObligations.statement: durante and be-not-so-fearful still pin @red-cup-engineering/abrash 0.1.1 (and durante @lenticule-science/metrologic 0.1.1), so their vendored module graphs and import maps still resolve and both are internally consistent AS PINNED. Carrying this migration into them requires publishing abrash 0.2.0, repinning both, replacing the @lenticule-science/metrologic/chu, /chu/four and /bilattice/charge import-map entries with @lenticule-science/articulating/predicating/positing/bilattice-charge, .../logic/linear-logic-chu and .../utterance (plus @red-cup-engineering/computer-data-type-engine/mark, articulating's only bare specifier), and rewriting durante's server.test.mts vendor-specifier list, which currently asserts a 200 on /vendor/@lenticule-science/metrologic/bilattice/src/charge.mjs — a file metrologic 0.3.0 no longer ships.
openObligations.whyNotDoneHere: durante's vendor route serves only .mjs and its server test asserts HTTP 200 on each import-map target without ever EXECUTING the page's module graph. That test can therefore be made green while the public page is actually broken, and no check available here (no browser) distinguishes the two. Shipping a half-vendored module graph to a public game face is worse than leaving both on their current, consistent pins. This is the same browser-delivery obligation recorded in 2026-09-10-metrologic-bilattice-charge-delegation.json, now also covering the chu specifiers.

openObligations.severity: needs a sibling agent's attention, not resolvable here
openObligations.statement: @lenticule-science/metrologic 0.3.0 was packed from a working tree that also carried another agent's in-flight edits to readout/, equality/, hyperdoctrine/, closure/ and obstruction/. A concurrent merge (merge normalize/ethereum-engineering-services-section) then reverted those files in the tree. The published 0.3.0 therefore contains source for those five surfaces that no longer exists on disk; only the chu-scoped files were restored here, from the published tarball.
openObligations.alsoObserved: metrologic's bilattice test suite (bilattice/test/*.test.mjs) currently fails to load because bilattice/src/charge.mjs is deleted in the working tree while its tests still import it — a sibling agent's half-landed charge-delegation cluster, untouched here.
